workflow.contradiction.committedNeedsFol.defaultMessage: “Committed is done” needs everyone in the project folder.
workflow.contradiction.committedNeedsFol.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: “Committed is done” was chosen while each card has its own folder.

workflow.contradiction.hiveMergesNeedsGi.defaultMessage: Merging needs Git: without version control, work is accepted where it is.
workflow.contradiction.hiveMergesNeedsGi.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a merge option was set for a project with no version control.

workflow.contradiction.mergeNeedsSlots.defaultMessage: When Hive or the agent merges, each card needs its own folder.
workflow.contradiction.mergeNeedsSlots.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a merging option was chosen while everyone works in the project folder.

workflow.contradiction.noneHasNoSlots.defaultMessage: Without version control, everyone works in the project folder.
workflow.contradiction.noneHasNoSlots.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: separate folders per card were set for a project with no version control.

workflow.contradiction.okWithReview.defaultMessage: Your OK before merging is already part of review by you.
workflow.contradiction.okWithReview.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: the user's OK before merging was set while the user already reviews.

workflow.contradiction.quorumNeedsAgent.defaultMessage: Two reviewers per card need review by reviewer agents.
workflow.contradiction.quorumNeedsAgent.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: two reviewers per card were set without reviewer agents.

workflow.contradiction.selfReview.defaultMessage: “Nobody reviews their own work” can't be off while a reviewer agent checks the work.
workflow.contradiction.selfReview.description: Why workflow options in the Version Control tab cannot be saved: the no-self-review option was turned off while a reviewer agent is required.

workflow.forYou.decidedAfterMerge.defaultMessage: {card} was decided after it merged: does it need a follow-up?
workflow.forYou.decidedAfterMerge.description: A For you request (Decide): a decision was recorded on the card while its work was being merged, so the merged work didn't see it. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.newDecision.defaultMessage: {card} has a new decision: your review again?
workflow.forYou.newDecision.description: A For you request: the user decided something new on a card in Review, so their review is asked again. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.okBefore.description: A For you request: the card passed review and waits for the user's OK before it merges (glossary 2.3: approval). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.passedReview.description: A For you request: reviewer agents passed the card, and the user reviews after them (A reviewer agent, then you). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.review.description: A For you request: the card waits for the user to review it (Version Control → Work is reviewed before it is merged: You). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.move.answer.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user's answer to a For you request (Approve, Decline, a reply).

workflow.move.declarePaths.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: saying which files are its work (a project without version control).

workflow.move.move.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: dragging it to another column.

workflow.move.putBack.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: putting a started card back in Todo.

workflow.move.removeFromQueue.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user taking it out of the merge queue.

workflow.move.reportMerge.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the agent saying it merged the work.

workflow.move.retryMerge.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user's Retry merge on the merge queue's card.

workflow.move.start.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move ("… isn't possible from there"): starting work on it.

workflow.move.startReview.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: a reviewer beginning a review.

workflow.move.submit.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: sending its work to Review.

workflow.move.verdict.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: a reviewer passing or failing it (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.refused.approval.given.change.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Your OK before merging.
workflow.refused.approval.given.change.description: Where the rule that waits for the user's OK is changed.

workflow.refused.approval.given.message.defaultMessage: {card} waits for the OK before merging.
workflow.refused.approval.given.message.description: A refused move: the user has to approve the card first (glossary 2.3: approval; Version Control → Your OK before merging).

workflow.refused.approval.given.next.defaultMessage: Wait for the OK, given on the card or in For you.
workflow.refused.approval.given.next.description: The next step after a move refused for want of the user’s approval.

workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.messag.defaultMessage: A plain number is not a card reference.
workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.messag.description: A refused intent: the card was named by a bare number.

workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.next.description: The forms a card reference takes: {key} like AM-12, {alias} like #1061.

workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..description: A refused check run: the revision named is not the checked-out one.

workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..defaultMessage: Run the check where {revision} is checked out, or without a revision.
workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..description: The next step after a check run named the wrong revision.

workflow.refused.done.contained.change.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Who merges.
workflow.refused.done.contained.change.description: Where the rule that checks a merge is changed.

workflow.refused.done.contained.message.description: A refused Done: the approved revision is not in the target branch. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.done.contained.next.defaultMessage: Merge {revision} into {target}, then report the merge again.
workflow.refused.done.contained.next.description: The next step after a refused report of a merge.

workflow.refused.evidence.changed.messag.defaultMessage: What Hive read for {card} changed while it decided.
workflow.refused.evidence.changed.messag.description: A refused intent: a branch head, a file or another card the rule depends on changed between Hive's reading it and recording the move. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.evidence.changed.next.defaultMessage: Try again: Hive reads it afresh.
workflow.refused.evidence.changed.next.description: The next step after a refusal because what a rule read changed meanwhile.

workflow.refused.integrate.approved.mess.description: A refused merge: the revision lacks the passes or approvals its rules need. {why} is a whole sentence saying what's missing.

workflow.refused.integrate.approved.next.description: The next step after a merge refused for want of approval.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Checks pass on the merged result.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..description: Where the merge checks are changed.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..defaultMessage: The merge checks failed on {card}'s merged result.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..description: A merge returned: the merge checks failed on the test merge.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..defaultMessage: Fix the failures, commit and submit the new revision.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..description: The next step after failed merge checks.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.chan.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Work is up to date before it merges.
workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.chan.description: Where the strict rule is changed.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.mess.description: A refused merge (strict): the revision is behind its target. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.next.defaultMessage: The merge queue brings it up to date itself.
workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.next.description: What happens next after the strict up-to-date rule refuses.

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.chan.defaultMessage: These rules are set in Version Control, where the user can change them.
workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.chan.description: Where the rules a move would skip are changed: the project's Version Control tab (a tab name: use it as Hive shows it).

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.mess.description: A move that skips rules: {rules} lists the rule names.

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.next.defaultMessage: Move it anyway only with the user's reason: one they gave for it, or one they give once told which rules this skips.
workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.next.description: The next step for a move that skips rules (said to the Hive Assistant): move anyway (an override) only with the user's own reason, given with the request or after being told which rules the move skips.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.messag.defaultMessage: {card} is in {stage}: {move} isn't possible from there.
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.messag.description: A refused intent: not possible from the stage the card is in. {stage} is a stage name, {move} the intent.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.next.description: The next step: the intents possible from the stage. {moves} lists them.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextNo.defaultMessage: Nothing waits to be done there now.
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextNo.description: The next step after a refused move when nothing is possible from the card's stage (the request it answered is no longer open).

workflow.refused.move.useIntent.message.defaultMessage: Agents don't move cards between columns.
workflow.refused.move.useIntent.message.description: A refused column move by an agent: agents act by intent.

workflow.refused.move.useIntent.next.description: The next step after a refused column move: {intent} is the intent to use.

workflow.refused.platform.unknown.messag.defaultMessage: {card}: Hive couldn't read {what}, so the rule {rule} can't be checked.
workflow.refused.platform.unknown.messag.description: A refused move: a fact a rule needs could not be read (git missing, folder gone). {what} says what, {rule} the rule id.

workflow.refused.platform.unknown.next.defaultMessage: Check Agent Setup or the folder, then try again.
workflow.refused.platform.unknown.next.description: The next step when Hive could not read what a rule needs.

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.change.defaultMessage: Retry merge on the merge queue retries it once.
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.change.description: Who can override a refused requeue: the user, with Retry merge on the merge queue (glossary 2.5: merge queue).

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.message.defaultMessage: {card} at {revision} can't go back into the merge queue unchanged: {why}
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.message.description: A refused resubmission into the merge queue. {card} is a card key, {revision} a short revision id, {why} one of the requeue reasons below, a whole sentence.

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.next.defaultMessage: Fix the failure, commit and submit the new revision.
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.next.description: The next step after a refused unchanged requeue.

workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.defaultMessage: {card} has a decision you haven't read.
workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.description: A refused review or verdict: the card has a newer decision than the reviewer has received.

workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.defaultMessage: Read it, judge whether the work meets it, then give your verdict.
workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.description: The next step after a refused verdict for an unread decision.

workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.mes.description: A refused review: the card has no submission.

workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.nex.defaultMessage: Wait for its builder to submit it.
workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.nex.description: The next step when there is nothing to review.

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.change.defaultMessage: Only Move anyway, on the card, skips this rule.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.change.description: Who can override the no-self-review rule: only the user, moving the card anyway (glossary 2.4: override, Move anyway).

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.messag.defaultMessage: You worked on {card}, so you can't review it.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.messag.description: A refused review: the reviewer is one of the agents who built the card.

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.next.defaultMessage: Leave the review to another reviewer.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.next.description: The next step after a refused self-review.

workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged.
workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.description: Where the rule that refused starting a card before the cards it waits for are done is changed.
A refused start of a card. {card} and {waitsFor} are card keys (AM-12): the card waits for {waitsFor}'s work to be merged or accepted.

workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.defaultMessage: Wait for {waitsFor} to be done, or work on another card.
workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.description: The next step after a refused start: {waitsFor} is the card key it waits for.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.change.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done.
workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.change.description: Where the rule that refused starting a blocked card is changed.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.messag.description: A refused start of a card. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {reason} is why the card is blocked, in the words given.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.next.defaultMessage: Wait for it to be unblocked, or work on another card.
workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.next.description: The next step after a refused start of a blocked card.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.cha.defaultMessage: This is set in Version Control → Where cards are built.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.cha.description: Where the rule that refused starting for want of a slot is changed.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.mes.defaultMessage: {card} can't start: no slot is free.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.mes.description: A refused start: every working folder (slot) is lent to other work. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.nex.defaultMessage: Wait for a slot to be free.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.nex.description: The next step after a refused start for want of a slot.

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.cha.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Checks pass before review.
workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.cha.description: Where the rule that refused a submit for a missing check is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.mes.description: A refused submit: a configured check has no passing counted run on the revision. {check} is the check name, {revision} a short revision id.

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.nex.description: The next step after a refused submit for a missing check: {command} is the command to run.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.change.defaultMessage: This rule comes with review and merging in Version Control.
workflow.refused.submit.clean.change.description: Where the rule that refused a submit with uncommitted changes comes from.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.message.defaultMessage: {card} can't go to review: {folder} has uncommitted changes ({files}).
workflow.refused.submit.clean.message.description: A refused submit: the working folder has uncommitted changes. {folder} is a folder path, {files} a list of file paths.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.next.defaultMessage: Commit your changes (or remove them), then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.clean.next.description: The next step after a refused submit with uncommitted changes.

workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.defaultMessage: {card} has a decision you haven't read.
workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.description: A refused submit: the card has a newer decision than the builder has received.

workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.defaultMessage: Read it, check your work against it, then submit.
workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.description: The next step after a refused submit for an unread decision.

workflow.refused.submit.empty.message.description: A refused submit: the change from the base is empty.

workflow.refused.submit.empty.next.description: The next step after submitting an empty change.

workflow.refused.submit.identity.change.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Commits use the project's identity.
workflow.refused.submit.identity.change.description: Where the identity rule is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.identity.message.defaultMessage: {card}: commit {commit} isn't authored with the project's identity ({email}).
workflow.refused.submit.identity.message.description: A refused submit: a commit's author email isn't the project's. {email} is the project's email address.

workflow.refused.submit.identity.next.defaultMessage: Set the identity, run {command}, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.identity.next.description: The next step after a refused submit for a commit's identity: {command} is the git command to fix it.

workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.mes.defaultMessage: {card} is already submitted at {revision} and waits for review or merging.
workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.mes.description: A refused submit: the same revision is already waiting. {card} is a card key, {revision} a short revision id.

workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.nex.defaultMessage: Wait for its review or merge.
workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.nex.description: The next step after a refused duplicate submission.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.c.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Agents stop what they started before review.
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.c.description: Where the rule about stopping runs before review is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.m.defaultMessage: {card}: runs you started are still going ({runs}).
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.m.description: A refused submit: the agent still has runs going. {runs} lists their titles.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.n.defaultMessage: Stop them or let them finish, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.n.description: The next step after a refused submit while runs are going.

workflow.refused.submit.ready.message.description: A refused submit: the revision stores conflicts. {files} lists file paths.

workflow.refused.submit.ready.next.defaultMessage: Resolve the conflicts, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.ready.next.description: The next step after a refused submit of a conflicted revision.

workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.description: A refused submit: the same revision again without a note.

workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.defaultMessage: Submit it again with a note saying what changed in your answer, or commit a new revision.
workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.description: The next step when submitting a reviewed revision again.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.change.defaultMessage: Each card in its own folder needs no trailers: Version Control → Where cards are built.
workflow.refused.submit.trailer.change.description: Where the setting that needs commit trailers is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.message.defaultMessage: {card}: commit {commit} has no card trailer, and another card's agent works in this folder.
workflow.refused.submit.trailer.message.description: A refused submit in a shared folder: a commit lacks the Hive-Card trailer. {commit} is a short commit id.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.next.description: The next step after a refused submit for a missing trailer: {command} is the git command to run.

workflow.refused.verdict.currentSubmissi.description: A refused verdict: it names an older submission. {submission} is its number.
The next step after a verdict on an old submission: {latest} is the latest submission number.

workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.messa.defaultMessage: You haven't started a review of {card}'s submission {submission}.
workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.messa.description: A refused verdict: the reviewer never started reviewing that submission. {submission} is its number.

workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.next.defaultMessage: Start the review first, then give your verdict.
workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.next.description: The next step after a verdict without a started review.

workflow.refused.why.passes.defaultMessage: {n, number} of {q, plural, one {# reviewer} other {# reviewers}} passed it.
workflow.refused.why.passes.description: The {why} of a refused merge: not enough distinct reviewers passed the revision. {n} and {q} are numbers.

workflow.refused.why.requeueLimit.defaultMessage: it was sent back unchanged {n, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} already.
workflow.refused.why.requeueLimit.description: The {why} of a refused requeue: the limit of unchanged requeues was reached. {n} is how many.

workflow.refused.why.requeueNotTransient.defaultMessage: its last merge failed for a reason in the work (a conflict, red checks or a hook), which needs a new revision.
workflow.refused.why.requeueNotTransient.description: The {why} of a refused requeue: the merge failure wasn't transient. Starts lower case: it follows a colon.

workflow.refused.why.stale.description: The {why} of a refused merge or requeue: the revision's pass no longer holds.

workflow.refused.why.userOk.defaultMessage: it waits for the OK before merging.
workflow.refused.why.userOk.description: The {why} of a refused merge: the user's approval is missing.

workflow.rule.approval.given.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G10).

workflow.rule.done.contained.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: a card is done only when its work is in its target (glossary 2.6: G5).

workflow.rule.integrate.approved.defaultMessage: Work is reviewed before it's merged
workflow.rule.integrate.approved.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G1).

workflow.rule.integrate.checksPassed.defaultMessage: Checks pass on the merged result
workflow.rule.integrate.checksPassed.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G9).

workflow.rule.integrate.upToDate.defaultMessage: Work is up to date before it merges
workflow.rule.integrate.upToDate.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G8, without the branch name).

workflow.rule.requeue.allowed.defaultMessage: Unchanged work is queued again only after a failure outside it
workflow.rule.requeue.allowed.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: work goes back into the merge queue unchanged only after a merge failed for a reason outside the work (a network error, a timeout).

workflow.rule.review.decisionsReceived.defaultMessage: The reviewer has read every decision
workflow.rule.review.decisionsReceived.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.5: reviewer).

workflow.rule.review.notAuthor.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N2, G2).

workflow.rule.start.dependenciesIntegrat.defaultMessage: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done
workflow.rule.start.dependenciesIntegrat.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N6, G14).

workflow.rule.start.notBlocked.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.start.slotAvailable.defaultMessage: Each card in its own folder
workflow.rule.start.slotAvailable.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G11 values): a card starts only when a folder is free.

workflow.rule.submit.checksPassed.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N3, G3).

workflow.rule.submit.clean.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.submit.decisionsReceived.defaultMessage: The builder has read every decision
workflow.rule.submit.decisionsReceived.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: the agent who built the card has read every decision on it (glossary 2.5: builder).

workflow.rule.submit.identity.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G12).

workflow.rule.submit.notDuplicate.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: the same revision isn't submitted twice.

workflow.rule.submit.ownRunsStopped.defaultMessage: Agents stop what they started before review
workflow.rule.submit.ownRunsStopped.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G13).

workflow.rule.submit.ready.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.submit.trailer.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: in a shared folder, each commit names its card.

workflow.rule.verdict.currentSubmission.defaultMessage: A verdict is on the latest submission
workflow.rule.verdict.currentSubmission.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.rule.verdict.reviewing.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: a reviewer starts a review before giving a verdict (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.stage.defaultMessage: {stage, select, hold {On Hold} todo {Todo} active {Active} review {Review} approved {Approved} merging {Merging} done {Done} other {{stage}}}
workflow.stage.description: A stage of the board, named in a refusal (glossary 2.2: On Hold, Todo, Active, Review, Approved, Merging, Done): translate each as the glossary does.

workflow.unreadable.branch.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …". {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.branchedOff.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the commit two lines of work have in common. {a} and {b} are commit ids or branch names.

workflow.unreadable.branchedOffTarget.defaultMessage: where the work branched off its target
workflow.unreadable.branchedOffTarget.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the commit the card's work and the branch it merges into have in common.

workflow.unreadable.cardPathsFiles.defaultMessage: the card's paths: they hold over {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
workflow.unreadable.cardPathsFiles.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the files a card names hold too many files. {n} is the limit.

workflow.unreadable.cardPathsSize.defaultMessage: the card's paths: they hold over {n, number} GB
workflow.unreadable.cardPathsSize.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the files a card names are too large. {n} is a size in gigabytes (GB, of 1024 MB): write the unit as your language does.

workflow.unreadable.change.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …" (glossary 2.3: change). {from} and {to} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.changeFingerprint.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": what tells a change apart from others (glossary 2.3: change).

workflow.unreadable.commitsOf.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …". {range} is a Git range of commits, like a1b2c3d..e4f5a6b.

workflow.unreadable.commitsOn.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …". {target} is a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.commitsSince.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …". {revision} and {base} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.contains.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …". {revision} and {target} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.defaultBranch.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the branch work merges into by default. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.deliverables.defaultMessage: the work in {project}: it has over {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
workflow.unreadable.deliverables.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": a project without version control has too many files to read its work. {project} is a project name, {n} the limit.

workflow.unreadable.files.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the files as they are at a revision. {revision} is a commit id or name.

workflow.unreadable.filesChanged.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …". {from} and {to} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.folderFor.description: What Hive couldn't make, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": a working folder (a Git worktree) for a branch. {branch} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.gitFolder.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the repository's .git folder. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.head.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the commit checked out in a folder, or at the tip of a branch. {where} is a folder path or a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.history.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the commits of a branch. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.holdsChange.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": whether the card's change is already in a commit or branch (glossary 2.3: change). {where} is a short commit id or a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.ignored.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the files Git is told to leave out. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.line.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": a Git branch. {branch} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.pathOutside.defaultMessage: the path {path}, which is outside the project
workflow.unreadable.pathOutside.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": a card's path that isn't in its project. {path} is the path.

workflow.unreadable.replay.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the result of applying a revision's change onto another commit. {revision} and {onto} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.replayedFiles.defaultMessage: the files of the change applied again
workflow.unreadable.replayedFiles.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the result of applying the change again on another commit, to tell whether two revisions are the same change.

workflow.unreadable.revision.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …" (glossary 2.3: revision). {revision} is a commit id or name.

workflow.unreadable.revisionIn.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the revision checked out in a folder (glossary 2.3: revision). {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.state.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": whether a merge or rebase is going on in the folder. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.target.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the branch the work merges into. {target} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.uncommitted.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …". {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.worktrees.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": the Git worktrees of a repository. {folder} is its folder path.

workflow.unreadable.writes.description: What Hive couldn't read, the object of "Hive couldn't read …": which files changed in a folder. {folder} is a folder path.
